learningObjectives: Understand the basic concepts behind TestSheets.
Identify the differences between Attributes and Instances.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Scenario: Testing the Shirt Size Selector

elements.text: You must test the Shirt Size field on the DemoWebShop: log in, navigate to Apparel & Shoes, select the "Men's Wrinkle Free Long Sleeve" shirt, and choose a size to add it to the cart. You need to check that all valid sizes (S, M, L) work, and that an invalid size (XL — not available for this shirt) correctly returns an error.

elements.description: The basic framework of TestCase-Design. A TestSheet is a central, structured repository of test data — Attributes and Instances — that specifies every combination you need to test. Think of it as a high-level guide through one slice of your SUT. Double-click the TestSheet symbol in the Navigation pane to view its contents.

elements.title: Create a TestSheet
items: Right-click the TestCaseDesign folder → Create TestSheet.
The TestSheet starts empty — it needs Attributes and Instances added manually.
In real projects this is normally done by a Test Design Specialist, using values specified by the Business department.

elements.description: Express a feature of a person or thing (e.g. a laptop's Attributes might be design or price; a person's might be hair color or height). Represented by a red square icon. An Attribute also acts as an organizational element for its child/sub-attributes.

The different variants of an Attribute (e.g. hair color Instances could be blond, brown, black). Represented by a flat white box with a capital "I". Instances have two roles: at the TestSheet level they represent individual TestCases; under an Attribute, they represent that Attribute's specific variant.

elements.caption: Our finished TestSheet: 1 Attribute (Size), 4 Instances (S, M, L valid + XL invalid). Each Instance column becomes one TestCase.

elements.text: If you can only see Attributes and not Instances, press F9 — it hides/unhides all Instances in the TestCaseDesign (red) section of Tosca.

elements.title: Add Attributes and Instances
items: Right-click the TestSheet or an Attribute → Create Attribute (or Create Instance).
Add the Instances at the TestSheet level first — this creates a new column per Instance, representing the TestCases to build.
Instance values can be entered manually on the Instance itself.
On the Attribute level, once at least 1 Instance exists, values become selectable from a drop-down.

elements.description: The leftmost column of a TestSheet is called "ValidValues" — the most important, most frequently used, or easiest path with the least dependencies (similar to the "Happy Path" concept). In Tosca terminology this column is the StraightThrough.

elements.text: Invalid Instance ≠ Failed TestCase. A TestCase FAILS when the actual SUT values differ from what's expected. An Invalid Instance simply verifies that the SUT correctly rejects a bad value (shows the right error message) — if the error message appears as expected, that TestCase PASSES. It would only fail if the SUT incorrectly accepted the invalid value (e.g. let you order a size that doesn't exist).

bulletPoints: Our final TestSheet: 3 valid Instance columns (S, M, L) + 1 invalid column (XL) = 4 TestCases to create.
This TestSheet is now ready to be linked to a Template (next lesson).

examPitfalls.title: Confusing an Invalid Instance with a failing TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume any TestCase built from an 'invalid' Instance is expected to fail.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: An Invalid Instance TestCase PASSES when the SUT correctly shows the expected error message. It only FAILS if the SUT incorrectly accepts the invalid value.

examPitfalls.title: Not knowing the F9 shortcut
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Learners can't find Instances in a limited TestCaseDesign view and assume the TestSheet is broken.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Press F9 in the TestCaseDesign (red) section to show/hide all Instances alongside Attributes.

examPitfalls.title: Mixing up Attribute and Instance icons
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates can't tell which element is an Attribute vs an Instance when reading a TestSheet.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Attribute = red square icon (describes a feature). Instance = flat white box with a capital 'I' (a specific variant/value of that feature).

examPitfalls.title: Adding Instances at the wrong level
examPitfalls.trapDescription: In the Log In Data exercise, candidates add User1/User2/User3 as Instances under an Attribute (like Email) instead of on the TestSheet itself, and then can't figure out why the grid doesn't show separate user columns.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Instances added directly on the TestSheet (right-click the TestSheet itself) represent the individual TestCases/users — e.g. User1, User2, User3. Instances added under an Attribute represent that Attribute's specific values.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is a TestSheet in Tosca terminology?

options.text: The basic framework of TestCase-Design, made of Attributes and Instances that specify the combinations to test.
A report generated only after ExecutionList runs.
A spreadsheet exported from Excel that Tosca cannot edit directly.
A single TestCase renamed for reuse.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's created inside the TestCaseDesign folder.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TestSheet is the basic framework of TestCase-Design: Attributes and Instances, in a structured way, specify the different combinations of TestCases needed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a TestSheet, what does an Attribute represent, and what icon is used?

options.text: A specific variant of a feature; represented by a white box with an 'I'.
A feature of a person/thing (e.g. Size); represented by a red square icon.
A TestStepValue reference; shown as a blue square.
The name of the ExecutionList; no icon is shown.

practiceQuiz.hint: Instances are the variants; Attributes are the features.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An Attribute expresses a feature (e.g. Size, hair color) and is shown as a red square icon. Instances (white box, capital 'I') are the variants of that Attribute (e.g. S, M, L, XL).

practiceQuiz.scenario: You built a TestCase for an Invalid Instance (ordering a shirt size that doesn't exist, XL). When you run it, the SUT correctly displays 'Size not available'. What is the result?

options.text: The result is inconclusive and must be manually reviewed every time.
The TestCase FAILS, because an Invalid Instance always causes a TestCase failure.
The TestCase is skipped automatically.
The TestCase PASSES, because the SUT correctly rejected the invalid value as expected.

practiceQuiz.hint: Failing = actual values differ from expected. Here, the expected outcome (rejection) occurred.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An Invalid Instance TestCase passes when the SUT behaves as expected — i.e., correctly rejects the invalid value with the right error message. It only fails if the SUT wrongly accepts the bad value.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You only see Attributes in the TestCaseDesign section, not the Instances beneath them. How do you reveal the Instances?

options.text: Instances cannot be hidden; something else is wrong.
Right-click the TestSheet and select 'Refresh'.
Press F9 to toggle Instance visibility.
Restart Tosca Commander.

practiceQuiz.rationale: F9 hides/unhides all Instances in the TestCaseDesign (red) section of Tosca.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the leftmost column of a TestSheet called, and what does it represent?

options.text: 'ValidValues' — the StraightThrough / Happy Path, the most-used combination with the least dependencies.
'Verification' — it only holds expected output values.
'ExecutionList' — it links directly to the Execution section.
'Defaults' — a column Tosca auto-generates and cannot be edited.

practiceQuiz.hint: Also known in Tosca terminology by another name.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The leftmost column, ValidValues, represents the StraightThrough (Happy Path) — the easiest, most representative combination with the fewest dependencies.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where do you create a new TestSheet, and how?

options.text: TestSheets are auto-generated the first time a Template is instantiated.
Right-click the TestCaseDesign folder → Create TestSheet.
Import it directly from an Excel file — Tosca cannot create one natively.
Right-click the ExecutionList folder → Create TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.hint: It lives in the TestCaseDesign section, alongside Attributes and Instances.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TestSheet is created by right-clicking the TestCaseDesign folder and selecting Create TestSheet, then manually adding Attributes and Instances.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What are the keyboard shortcuts to create a new Attribute and a new Instance, respectively?

options.text: Ctrl+A for a new Attribute; Ctrl+I for a new Instance (no prefix needed).
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T for both — Tosca does not differentiate the two.
F9 for a new Attribute; F10 for a new Instance.
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A for a new Attribute; Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I for a new Instance.

practiceQuiz.hint: Both start with the same Ctrl+N prefix, then a second letter to specify what's being created.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A creates a new Attribute; Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I creates a new Instance — both are shown in the official Exercise 1 (Log In Data TestSheet) instructions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Log In Data exercise, you need 3 separate test users (User1, User2, User3), each with their own Email and Password. Where do you create the User1/User2/User3 Instances?

options.text: In a separate TestSheet, one per user.
Directly on the TestSheet itself (not under the Email or Password Attribute).
Under the Password Attribute only.
Under the Email Attribute only.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the same distinction as 'Instance on TestSheet level = TestCase' from the core lesson.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Instances created directly on the TestSheet (right-click the TestSheet itself) represent the individual TestCases/users — User1, User2, User3. The Email/Password Instances underneath the Attributes hold each user's specific values, set via drop-down in the TestSheet grid.

quickRecap.value: Central, structured repository of test data (Attributes + Instances) for TestCase-Design.
A feature (red square icon) — e.g. Size.
A variant of an Attribute (white box, capital 'I') — e.g. S, M, L, XL.
Toggles Instance visibility in the TestCaseDesign section.
Leftmost column — the Happy Path, least dependencies.
An Invalid Instance TestCase PASSES if the SUT correctly rejects it.
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A = new Attribute. Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I = new Instance.
Instance on the TestSheet itself = a TestCase/user. Instance under an Attribute = that Attribute's value.
